posts.author: Jeffrey Weil
posts.content_md:
Hello Everyone,

I'm looking for a small simple laminator like this

[http://www.mbkpinternational.com/perfec ... inator.htm](http://www.mbkpinternational.com/perfect_cl25_cold_laminator.htm)

but smaller. I only need a little more than 8 inches wide. I want something simple like this for laminating film to glass. A motor on it would be nice too or I'll have to add it on myself.

If anyone has something to sell or knows of a new source please let me know.

 Jeffrey Weil

 NorthBeach Holography Inc.

posts.author: Jeffrey Weil
posts.content_md:
Hello Sergio,

Thanks but thats not the type I need. That's a hot laminator. The same but different. There is no way to adjust the distance between the rollers on that type. Glass will be too thick. You can see the adj. knobs on the top sides in the one I made reference to.

Also the rollers are recessed inside the shell. I need to have access to the rollers themselves to get the lamination right. 

Thanks for the help though.

 Jeff Weil

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md: Once in a while Aldi sells a little pouch laminator for about $20 that might be hackable considering its price!

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: There was a thread a long time back discussing this very thing. I remember finding a pouch laminator on ebay just like the one I use as well. I cut the cover off, removed the little heating strip, and it works great for plates 8" wide. Easy enough to mess with the spring mounts to adjust the pressure. Can't beat the price with a stick!

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md:
Yes i purchased my laminator on the big"E", it was an older one with a hand crank (the motor wont burn out), well theoretically that is. i then built a small platform on each side to lay the plate on, then just crank it thru. Reversing the feed is easy to do too! 

it will only hold 1/8" glass with film. I don’t mount my film until after processing and trimming is done, as its easy enough to screw it up in the dark!
